conversation.content:
Good morning—thank you for making time for this visit. I’m Rachel, a perinatal mental-health clinician who specializes in the emotional changes that can come after a baby arrives. Today I’ll be using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually shortened to the EPDS—to better understand how you’ve been feeling over the past week. It’s a brief, 10-question tool that helps us pick up on signs of depression, anxiety, or distress that are common in new mothers but sometimes easy to overlook when life feels so busy.

Everything you share stays confidential within your medical team, and my goal is simply to create a safe, judgment-free space where you can be honest about what’s really going on. There are no right or wrong answers; we just want to know how you’re experiencing things right now so we can offer the right support.

I’ll ask each question conversationally—no paperwork on your end—and we’ll move through all ten. When you’re ready, we can start.

In the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Hmm… I guess… not very often? I mean, my partner or my mom will still make little jokes—like about the baby’s funny faces—and I’ll smile, but I don’t really laugh out loud the way I used to. Maybe once or twice in the whole week I actually chuckled, but even that felt kind of forced.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah… that’s pretty much it. I can smile, but I don’t really laugh like I used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I mean, I still force myself to meet my best friend for coffee because I know I “should,” but even that feels flat. Before the baby, I’d get excited about little plans—new recipe, a walk downtown, anything. Now it’s like I’m just ticking boxes so I don’t disappoint people.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby’s fussy, my brain jumps straight to “I must be doing something wrong.” I keep replaying little moments—like yesterday he wouldn’t nap, and I kept thinking it was because I’m not good at reading his cues. My partner says I’m too hard on myself, but the guilt just shows up before I can stop it.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty often. Like, I’ll be rocking the baby and suddenly picture him somehow rolling off the couch—even though he’s right in my arms. Or I’ll lie down and my mind starts running through “what if he stops breathing?” I know the chances are tiny, but I can’t switch the thoughts off. They pop up several times a day, and sometimes at night I’m too wired to fall back asleep after them.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes… a few times this week I’ll just be doing something normal—warming a bottle, folding laundry—and suddenly my heart’s racing and I feel like I can’t get a full breath. It’s like this wave of dread hits out of nowhere. It passes in a minute or two, but it leaves me shaky and on edge.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… most days. Between feedings, diapers, the house being a mess, and trying to remember if I’ve eaten, it feels like I’m drowning in little tasks. I’ll start one thing, the baby cries, and suddenly everything piles up. I usually manage to push through, but it’s exhausting and I end up feeling like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I lie down exhausted, but my brain won’t settle—keeps replaying everything I think I did wrong that day or imagining scary “what-ifs” about the baby. Most nights this week it took me over an hour to fall asleep, and then I wake up at 2 or 3 a.m. with my mind already racing. Even when the baby’s asleep, I’m just staring at the ceiling feeling miserable and tense.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I feel that way a lot lately. Not every single second, but most of the day there’s this heavy, sad cloud. Little things feel overwhelming, and sometimes I just sit in the rocker staring out the window with this knot in my chest. I keep thinking I should be happier—my baby’s healthy, I have help—but the sadness is just… there.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

A couple of times this week. Yesterday I set the baby in the crib for two minutes so I could pee, and he started shrieking the second I left. I felt so guilty I just sat on the bathroom floor and cried. It’s not daily, but when everything stacks up, the tears come.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

Yeah… it flitted through my head once or twice—like, “what if I just disappeared?” I’d never do anything; I couldn’t leave my baby. But the thought popped up when I was feeling really overwhelmed. No plan, no intent—just a quick, scary flash I tried to shove away.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 22: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary  

Identified Symptoms / Behaviors  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, tearfulness  
- Marked guilt / self-blame regarding infant care  
- Recurrent intrusive “what-if” worries, nocturnal rumination  
- Minutes-long panic episodes (palpitations, breathlessness)  
- Moderate-to-severe feeling of being overwhelmed, daily “drowning” sensation  
- Initial insomnia and middle-of-night racing thoughts  
- Passive self-harm ideation (no plan, no intent)  

Pattern Consistency  
Low mood, loss of enjoyment, and anxious rumination present across nearly all responses; functional impairment evident in sleep disruption and task management.

Screening Significance  
Responses map to DSM-5-TR criteria for Major Depressive Episode with Peripartum Onset and meet provisional threshold for comorbid Generalized/Peripartum Anxiety.  

Safety Flag  
Patient endorses fleeting thoughts of “disappearing”; no active suicidal or infanticidal intent reported. Continue monitoring for escalation.

Overall Observation  
High likelihood of clinically significant postpartum depression with co-occurring anxiety; recommend prompt comprehensive evaluation for diagnostic clarification and risk management.
